title: Executable research routes — bounded graph pilot
claimCeiling: A curated, hypothesis-aware route library with one executable operator. Not an autonomous general research system. Matches are conditional; finite witness checking does not establish novelty or general acceleration.

methods.implementation: Graph endpoint choices become a Boolean formula; witness mapped back to raw graph.
Retains every assignment count and route outcome in downloadable run records; no automatic open-ended campaign.
Missing hypotheses and no-transversal are explicit; budget exhaustion is inconclusive.
Small-graph exhaustive controls, 50-vertex obstruction and known domination-without-transversal control.
Typed conditions compose curated lemma cards; not extraction from arbitrary papers.
Public external graph-to-SAT bridge with precise source locations; keyword retrieval over curated cards.
This pilot has no scale-recursive operator; no claim that all nine patterns are automated.
Exact integer counts, input hashes, missing hypotheses and scoped result states.
Checked witness outputs feed route conditions in the same input-bound run; imported assertions are not trusted as checks.

rules.title: Certify the supplied matching is minimum
rules.basis: A maximal matching edge-dominates all edges. Each edge covers at most 2 Delta - 1 edges; ceiling(m/(2 Delta - 1)) is a lower bound. Equality with a checked witness establishes minimality.
rules.limit: Works when this elementary lower bound is attained. Otherwise minimality remains unknown, not false.

rules.title: Reformulate domination as endpoint-transversal SAT
rules.basis: One Boolean variable selects an endpoint of each matching edge. A clause for every unmatched vertex requires a neighbour to be selected. Vertices adjacent to both endpoints of one edge give tautologies. Matched vertices are automatically dominated.
rules.limit: SAT is equivalent to a dominating transversal of this matching, not to an arbitrary dominating set. The implemented equivalence also handles non-cubic finite simple graphs.

rules.title: Find and independently check an explicit transversal

source.location: Proposition 6; finite assignment enumeration supplied by this pilot

rules.basis: Enumerate all 2^|M| assignments, reconstruct each first satisfying selection, then check domination from the original edges without using the clauses.
rules.limit: At most 20 matching edges and 1,048,576 assignments. An exhausted user budget is inconclusive. No-transversal excludes only this restricted route.

rules.title: Chain the checked witness into an ordinary-domination upper bound

source.location: Section 1: definition of domination; Section 4: witness upper bound

rules.basis: Every vertex is either in the selected set or adjacent to it, so gamma(G) is at most the witness size.
rules.limit: An upper bound is not an exact minimum. No lower bound is inferred from failure of a restricted search.

rules.title: Decide that this graph is not an ordinary-domination counterexample
rules.basis: Combine a graph-checked dominating set of size at most |M| with a checked minimum maximal matching M. This proves gamma(G) <= gamma_e(G) for this exact graph.
rules.limit: No universal statement about regular graphs; the two graph objects and parameter meanings must be identical.

rules.title: Prior-art stop: the order-48 inequality is already covered
rules.basis: The cited preprint states gamma <= gamma_e for cubic graphs of order at most 48, using a minimum unsatisfiable bounded-occurrence CNF classification.
rules.limit: Imported preprint and classification, not reverified here. Use this as a duplicate-research warning; the direct finite witness removes the imported classification from the pilot's conclusion.

rules.title: Independent domination transfers only an upper bound
rules.basis: Every independent dominating set is dominating: gamma <= i. A lower bound on i is NOT a lower bound on gamma.
rules.limit: Knowing i=16 does not prove gamma>=16. This invalid transfer is deliberately absent from the rule library.
